probe_result: In a serialized single-writer symbolic recurrence with deterministic transition identity deliberately unavailable, a replicated two-copy predecessor-bound write-ahead intent journal preserved zero false orphan adoption/stale regression across nine tested corruption/loss cases and automatically continued all six non-ambiguous useful-continuation cases. A single capsule continued four of six; generation-embedded self-certification alone continued one of six because child integrity does not identify which child was intended.
neuroscience_transfer: Recurrence recovery should separate an intention-selection cue from reinstatement-content integrity. Redundant prospective-intent traces can tolerate loss of one trace, but familiarity with a surviving orphan representation is not evidence of which intention was active; conflicting cues should suppress reinstatement rather than force a guess.
mechanism_revision: Use two certificates: replicate a pre-effect selection certificate across two independently verifiable intent slots, then use successor-embedded self-certification only as a post-selection integrity check. Restart reads current first, requires at least one valid current-predecessor intent and no conflicting same-predecessor intent, repairs redundancy, verifies successor agreement, and only then commits current. Unique-intent uncertainty remains fail-closed.
scope_guard: Positive evidence is limited to nine serialized single-writer symbolic cases with immutable generations, one atomic current pointer, independently verifiable immutable intent records, no forged-valid corruption, and no deterministic transition identity. No claim for concurrent writers, non-atomic current mutation, double intent-copy loss, journal rollover/ABA, or adversarial hash collisions.
